A notable challenge for the government is the control of the public wage bill, which is

much larger than in other PICs [Pacific Island countries], even though the total share of] public employment is similar. The IMF noted that wages constitute about half of

recurrent government expenditures, and that the public wage bill increased from 10.5

percent of GDP in 2005 to 12.0 percent of GDP in 2008. By their nature, public health

and education spending involve significant wage shares.

At the same time, the share of government financing to community health centers has fallen from

21.6 percent of the government's health budget in 2006 to 18.1 percent in 2010 (Government of

Vanuatu, 2011c). Additional funding from development partners has helped to maintain some

service-level capacity in rural areas.
